_what_this_is: Which doorways name an act their children do not model. A student can hold every child and still fail the question, and nothing in the graph can express why - the walk cannot find it, because the act sits at the doorway and the doorway is never asked about.
_how_it_was_made: Found by a tutor watching a student on 2026-09-02: a subtraction question traced correctly to what a fraction is and back up, and the student still could not do it, because nothing tested combining the numerators over the shared denominator. A lexical rule - probe contains 'then' or 'and simplify' - was tried first and rejected: it flags 5 of 70 doorways and misses the founding case entirely, because 'Add or subtract two fractions with different denominators' promises nothing and hides everything. So every doorway was judged semantically in one pass, on claude-opus-5, 2026-09-02.
_what_it_is_not: Not a list of nodes to add. Twenty-four entries is a third of the graph and adding them unexamined would be a larger unvalidated expansion than the one this exists to correct. It is a backlog, ordered by whatever outside evidence turns up. Two have been acted on: combine_over_common_denominator, from the tutor session, and set_derivative_zero, from Cambridge 9709 March 2025 P1 Q2(b).
_calibration: add_subtract_fractions is the anchor: its act provably has a child, because a tutor found the gap on 2026-09-02 and combine_over_common_denominator was added for it. A run that calls it unmodelled is not trusted and writes nothing. expand_brackets was the second anchor until 2026-09-18, when re-judging showed the original verdict had named only the collecting half of its probe and never judged the multiplication - so it was never evidence the judge gets that doorway right. An anchor has to be checkable without trusting the run it checks.

add_subtract_fractions.act: Combine numerators over the shared denominator

evidence.detail: A tutor watched a student climb the whole chain - what a fraction is, equivalent fractions, finding a common denominator - and still fail the subtraction. Nothing tested combining the numerators over the shared denominator. Fixed by combine_over_common_denominator.

area_between_curves.act: Integrate the difference of the two functions
area_between_curves.missing: Needs a node for forming the integrand as (upper curve − lower curve) over the intersection limits. A student can find the meeting points (solve_quadratic) and evaluate any integral handed to them (definite_integral) and still integrate each curve separately and subtract answers in the wrong order, or subtract lower−upper and report a negative area.

area_under_curve.act: Set up and evaluate the integral for the area

arithmetic_sequence.act: Recover a and d from two given terms
arithmetic_sequence.missing: Needs a node for turning two given terms into two equations in a and d and eliminating one (simultaneous equations from sequence terms). Knowing what an nth term rule does does not stop a student writing the two terms with the same n, or subtracting to get d and then forgetting to back-substitute for a.

arithmetic_series_sum.missing: Needs a node for the sum formula itself, Sn = n/2(2a + (n−1)d) (or n/2(a+l)), and choosing it over the nth-term rule. The classic error — computing the nth term and calling it the sum, or using n rather than n/2 — has nowhere to live.

binomial_approximation.act: Choose the substitution value that produces the target number
binomial_approximation.missing: Needs a node for selecting x so that the expanded expression equals the required root (e.g. solving 1 + 2x = 1.02 to get x = 0.01) before substituting. With only coefficients, validity and substitution as children, a student who picks the wrong x — substituting the target value itself — fails with no node to blame.

binomial_validity.act: State and justify the range of validity

classify_stationary.act: Evaluate the second derivative and conclude max or min

compare_standard_form.act: Order numbers in standard form by comparing powers first and mantissas only as a tie-break
compare_standard_form.missing: A node would have to test the comparison rule itself: that between two numbers in standard form the one with the larger index is larger regardless of the front number, and that the mantissas decide only when the indices are equal (with negative indices ordered as negatives). A student who knows standard_form_meaning, power_of_ten and negatives can still place 3.1x10^4 above 2.9x10^5 by reading the leading digits, or reverse the order of 5x10^-3 and 2x10^-6 by treating -6 as 'bigger'.

complete_the_square.act: Form (x + b/2)^2 and correct the constant
complete_the_square.missing: Needs a node for the completing step: halve the x-coefficient, square the bracket, then subtract (b/2)^2 and combine with c. Expanding, factorising and negatives are all ingredients; x^2+6x+1 → (x+3)^2+1 (forgetting to subtract 9) is the standard error and nothing in the children tests it.

connected_rates.missing: Needs a node for assembling the chain of rates, dV/dt = dV/dr × dr/dt: identifying which rate is given, which is wanted, and that the shared variable cancels. Chain rule as a differentiation technique does not catch a student who divides the rates or multiplies the wrong pair.

direct_proportion.act: Scale via the value of one

evaluate_composite.act: Substitute one function into the other in the right order

evaluate_definite_integral.act: Evaluate between limits in exact form

evaluate_index.act: Evaluate a number to a negative/fractional/zero power

expand_binomial.act: Assemble the terms of the expansion

expand_binomial_fractional.act: Build the first few terms with a negative/fractional index

expand_brackets.act: Multiply every term of the first bracket by every term of the second
expand_brackets.missing: A node would have to test the exhaustive pairing of terms across two brackets - that (a+b)(c+d) produces four products before any collecting. expand_single_bracket only tests one bracket times one term, and collect_like_terms only tidies what is already there. A student who holds both can write (2x+3)(x-5) = 2x^2 - 15, multiplying only first-with-first and last-with-last.
expand_brackets.note: Re-judged 2026-09-18. The 2026-09-02 pass recorded this as modelled with the act named 'Collect the expanded result', which is the second half of its own probe; the multiplication was never judged. Suspected only - no node added, and no outside confirmation yet.

factorise_common.act: Take out the HCF and write the correct bracket

factorise_cubic.act: Find the first factor, divide, factorise the rest
factorise_cubic.missing: Needs a node for locating the first root by testing candidate values (factors of the constant term) with f(a)=0. The factor theorem concept states what f(a)=0 means and division and quadratic factorising handle the rest, but a student who does not know which values to try, or who tests values unrelated to the constant term, has no node covering that search.

factorise_quadratic.act: Choose the factor pair and write the brackets

find_stationary_points.act: Solve f'(x)=0 and find the y-coordinates
find_stationary_points.missing: Needs a node for back-substituting each root into the ORIGINAL function to get the y-coordinate. Every child stops at the x-values; substituting the root into the derivative (getting y = 0 every time) is a common and currently undiagnosable error.

evidence.detail: Cambridge 9709 March 2025 P1 Q2(b): candidates differentiated dy/dx again instead of setting it to zero. Half fixed by set_derivative_zero; the other half - substituting the roots back into the ORIGINAL function for the y-coordinates - is still open, which is why this stays on the backlog.

first_principles.act: Form and simplify the difference quotient, then take the limit
first_principles.missing: Needs a node for setting up [f(x+h) − f(x)]/h from the function. Children give the limit concept, expanding and algebraic fractions, but writing f(x+h) correctly (e.g. expanding (x+h)^2 as x^2+h^2) and cancelling the h before taking the limit is untested.

form_and_solve.act: Form an equation and solve it

form_simultaneous_from_context.act: Turn one situation into two equations in the SAME two unknowns
form_simultaneous_from_context.missing: A node would have to test producing a consistent pair: defining the two letters once and writing each separate statement of the situation as its own equation in those same letters. form_expression_words only tests a single sentence to a single expression, and pair_of_unknowns only asks why two equations are needed. A student holding all three can write one equation and then an incompatible second (redefining the letters, or restating the first equation in a rearranged form) so that elimination gives 0=0 or a meaningless answer.

fraction_of_amount.act: Compute a fraction of a quantity
fraction_of_amount.missing: Needs a procedure node for the operation itself: divide by the denominator and multiply by the numerator. The only child is the concept of what a fraction means; a student who divides 45 by 3 and stops, or divides by the numerator, fails with nothing to point at.

fractions_arith.act: Carry out the addition, multiplication or division
fractions_arith.missing: Needs the executing nodes as children — combining numerators over a common denominator, and multiplying numerators and denominators. As it stands the children are all preparation and concept, so 1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5 or multiplying tops and adding bottoms has no home (combine_over_common_denominator and multiply_divide_fractions exist in the graph but are not attached here).

geometric_sequence.act: Recover a and r from two given terms
geometric_sequence.missing: Needs a node for dividing one term by the other to eliminate a and find r, then back-substituting for a. Index laws and the nth-term concept do not catch a student who subtracts the terms (treating r like a common difference) or forgets to find a.

geometric_series_sum.missing: Needs a node for the sum formula a(1−r^n)/(1−r) and its use. Nothing tests writing the formula correctly: using r^n instead of 1−r^n, or dividing by r−1 with the numerator ordered the other way, is a standard error with nowhere to live.

implicit_diff.act: Differentiate y-terms w.r.t. x and rearrange for dy/dx
implicit_diff.missing: Needs a node for differentiating a term in y with respect to x, producing the dy/dx factor (d/dx of y^2 = 2y dy/dx), and then collecting all dy/dx terms on one side to make it the subject. Generic chain and product rules plus algebraic fractions do not catch the student who writes 2y with no dy/dx, or who never gathers the dy/dx terms.

increasing_decreasing.act: Solve the derivative inequality and state the interval
increasing_decreasing.missing: Needs a node for solving a quadratic inequality f'(x) > 0 and expressing the answer as a range. With only roots (solve_quadratic) and the sign concept, a student who reports the two roots, or gets the interval inside/outside the wrong way round, cannot be diagnosed.

inequality_on_number_line.act: Translate between an inequality and its number-line picture

integer_solutions.act: Enumerate the integers lying in a solved range, respecting which ends are included

integrate_by_substitution.act: Change the variable, the differential and the limits
integrate_by_substitution.missing: Needs a node for executing the substitution: du = ... dx, replacing dx, and converting the limits to the new variable. Recognising what to substitute and evaluating an integral do not cover the student who forgets to replace dx or keeps the original x-limits.

integrate_expression.act: Integrate term by term with + c

line_through_two_points.act: Find gradient then write the line

midpoint_and_distance.act: Apply the midpoint and distance formulas

multiply_divide_fractions.missing: Needs a node for the multiplying act itself: numerator times numerator, denominator times denominator (after flipping for a division). The children give the reciprocal concept, fraction meaning and simplifying; 2/3 × 4/5 = 8/8 or cross-multiplying has no node.

normal_equation.act: Negate-and-flip the tangent gradient and write the line

optimisation.act: Interpret the optimised result in context
optimisation.missing: Needs a node for converting the stationary x back into the quantity asked for — substituting into the original function to give the maximum area/volume, and checking it against the context. As built, a student can form and optimise the function and answer with x = 4 instead of the maximum volume, with nothing to record that.

order_fdp.act: Convert to a common form and order

parametric_diff.missing: Needs a node for assembling dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt). Differentiating each parametric equation and simplifying fractions are ingredients; inverting the quotient (dx/dt over dy/dt) or multiplying the two derivatives is the actual error and it is untested.

percentage_change.act: Apply or find a percentage change

polynomial_division.missing: Needs a node for the division process itself — long division or matching coefficients: divide the leading term, multiply back, subtract, bring down the next term. Expanding, solving linear equations and negatives are all ingredients; sign errors at the subtraction step and dropping a missing power are the real failures and have no home.

rationalise_denominator.act: Multiply by the right form of 1
rationalise_denominator.missing: Needs a node for choosing and applying the multiplier — the surd itself, or the conjugate for a two-term denominator — to both numerator and denominator. Surds, algebraic fractions and expanding do not catch multiplying only the denominator, or using a+√b instead of the conjugate a−√b.

second_derivative.act: Differentiate twice and read the sign

share_in_ratio.act: Find one share of the total

simplify_index_expression.act: Combine into a single index form

simplify_logs.act: Apply the log laws in either direction

simplify_ratio.act: Divide both parts by the HCF

simultaneous_linear_quadratic.act: Substitute the line into the curve, solve, and pair each x with its own y

sketch_modulus_graph.act: Sketch and read off the vertex

solve_both_sides.act: Gather the unknown on one side

solve_exponential_equation.act: Take logs of both sides and bring the index down

solve_linear.act: Solve a one or two step equation

solve_linear_inequality.act: Run the equation-solving steps on an inequality, flipping the sign when required

solve_log_equation.act: Convert the log statement into index form
solve_log_equation.missing: Needs a node for the log-to-index conversion, log_a x = b ⇒ x = a^b, once the logs have been combined. Log laws, index laws and linear solving leave the student who writes x = b^a, or who cancels the 'log' from both sides, undiagnosed.

solve_modulus_equation.act: Take both branches and reject invalid roots
solve_modulus_equation.missing: Needs a node for splitting into the two cases (expression = +k and = −k) and then substituting back to reject solutions that do not satisfy the original modulus equation. modulus_meaning explains the notation only; giving just the positive branch, or keeping an extraneous root, has nowhere to live.

solve_quadratic.act: Set each factor to zero and give both roots

solve_quadratic_inequality.act: Find the critical values then choose the region(s) satisfying the inequality

solve_simultaneous_substitution.act: Replace a variable in the second equation by a whole EXPRESSION and simplify
solve_simultaneous_substitution.missing: A node would have to test substituting an algebraic expression (not a number) for a variable in another equation - bracketing it so that a coefficient multiplies the whole expression, then expanding and collecting. substitute_expr explicitly tests only putting a number in, and rearrange_formula stops at making y the subject. A student with every child can rearrange to y = 3 - 2x and then write 4y as 4*3 - 2x, or substitute back into the equation they rearranged and get an identity.

standard_form_add_subtract.act: Rewrite one number so both share the same power of ten before adding
standard_form_add_subtract.missing: A node would have to test the equalising step itself: converting 3.2x10^5 into 0.32x10^6 (or the reverse) so two standard-form numbers can be added, and only then adding the front numbers while keeping the shared power. Nothing in the graph does this - back_into_standard_form only tidies an answer afterwards, and power_of_ten only values a single power. A student holding every child can add 3.2x10^5 + 4x10^6 as 7.2x10^11 or 7.2x10^6.

standard_form_multiply_divide.act: Regroup as (front x front) x (power x power), using index laws on the powers

standard_form_to_ordinary.act: Shift the digits by the stated power of ten

state_domain_range.act: State a domain or range with justification

straight_line_equation.act: Write the line from a point and gradient

sum_to_infinity.missing: Needs a node for the sum-to-infinity formula and its evaluation. The children supply a and r, the fraction arithmetic and the validity condition, but nothing tests forming a/(1−r) — using a/(1+r), or r−1 in the denominator, especially with a negative r.

tangent_equation.act: Gradient at the point then the line

use_discriminant.act: Compute b^2−4ac and interpret the sign

use_factor_theorem.act: Substitute the root and solve for the constant

write_in_standard_form.act: Choose the mantissa between 1 and 10 and the matching index, sign included

_the_standing_rule: A new doorway is not finished until it has been judged here. The question is not 'are its prerequisites right' but 'if a student passed every one of them, could they now do the actual question, or is there an act nobody tested'. test_assembly.py fails on any doorway with no verdict, so this cannot be skipped by forgetting. See backend/assembly.py.
_how_the_backlog_is_ordered: By outside confirmation only, and it is derived rather than written down: recorded evidence in each entry, plus diagnoses marked wrong by a tutor on sessions that started at that doorway, which is what this fault looks like from outside. With nothing confirmed the order is alphabetical and means nothing, and the report says so rather than implying a priority.
